scores.claim_text: 914 warehouses worldwide at Aug 31 2025; 27 opened in FY25; up to 35 planned FY26.
scores.M_check: EDGAR fulltext for '914 warehouses' restricted to Costco CIK

M_value.filings: 10-K 2025-10-08 (the canonical disclosure) + two 2025-Q4 8-Ks (operating-results press releases dated 2025-09-25 and 2025-10-15)

scores.interpretation: The 914-warehouse number appears in three Costco-filed SEC documents within FY25-close period (the 10-K and two operating-results 8-Ks). Cross-disclosure consistency within the issuer's own filings is the strongest available corroboration for a store-count claim. Calibration 11 (store-count trajectory) satisfied: 861 -> 890 -> 914 implies +29 and +24 net additions; the 10-K explicitly reconciles to 27 openings + 3 relocations in FY25, which nets to ~24 new locations (consistent with the +24 net delta from 890 to 914). No M-side contradiction. CONTROL-baseline PASS.

scores.claim_text: $269.9B net sales FY25 / $275.2B total revenue; segment income $6.88B US, $1.85B Canada, $1.66B Other Intl; merchandise-category disaggregation.
scores.M_check: Counterparty cross-check via mall-REIT 10-Ks for tenant exposure to Costco

M_value.filings_range: Both REITs have multi-year cross-references; MAC's hits are concentrated in quarterly press-release 8-Ks (recurring tenant-line disclosure); SPG's hits include 10-Q tenant rosters.

scores.interpretation: Both major mall REIT counterparties name Costco multiple times across multi-year filings. Costco is generally a freestanding/power-center tenant (not a typical mall anchor), so REIT exposure is less load-bearing than e.g. for Macy's or Nordstrom. The cross-disclosure simply confirms Costco operates real, identifiable retail premises within the institutional commercial-real-estate ecosystem - i.e. it isn't a phantom store-count claim. Revenue-magnitude itself is internally-disclosed and not directly queryable via M-sources; segment-level granularity (US/Canada/Other Intl) plus disaggregated merchandise-category sales are auditor-attested KPMG figures with Item 8 attestation including ICFR. Calibration 9 (comp-store-sales test): MD&A is consistent with positive comp trajectory (rev growth 8.1% FY25 net of fuel/FX). No M-side red flag. CONTROL-baseline PASS.

scores.claim_text: Deferred membership fees $2,854M at FY25 end (up from $2,501M FY24, +14% YoY).
supports: filing self-disclosure (audited Note to Financial Statements)
scores.M_check: EDGAR fulltext for 'Costco membership' as a discriminative-phrase corroboration check + internal MD&A/Note consistency

M_value.edgar_external_corroboration: 5 hits - mostly Costco's own 10-Qs and 8-Ks (operating results); one external hit is Avis Budget Group's 10-K cross-referencing a Costco membership partnership (corroborates the membership program exists as a marketing asset visible to third-party SEC filers)
M_value.internal_consistency: Deferred membership fee balance 2,501 -> 2,854 is +14.1% YoY; rate of growth materially exceeds top-line revenue growth (~8%), consistent with the September 2024 fee increase (US Gold Star $60->$65, Executive $120->$130) flowing through deferred liability before fully recognizing on the income statement. KPMG audited.

scores.interpretation: Deferred membership fees are one of the framework's HIGH-rubric items (recurring-revenue, contractual, auditor-attested). The +14% YoY delta in the deferred liability is mechanically consistent with the membership-fee increase and ongoing membership-count growth. No M-side contradiction; magnitude is in line with disclosed paid-membership base (~77M households at year-end per Costco operating-results 8-Ks). CONTROL-baseline PASS.

scores.claim_text: Citibank, N.A. is exclusive issuer of US co-branded credit cards to Costco members.
scores.M_check: Counterparty cross-check via Citigroup (parent of Citibank N.A.) SEC filings; aggregate 'Costco co-branded' phrase counts; Visa control check

M_value.Citigroup_filing_distribution: Multiple 10-Ks (2018, 2019) and 10-Qs (2018, 2019, 2021, 2022) - recurring multi-year disclosure consistent with a long-standing material partner-card portfolio (Citi assumed the Costco Anywhere Visa portfolio from American Express in 2016)

scores.interpretation: STRONG counterparty corroboration via Citigroup (37 hits across years). Citi-side disclosure of Costco as a material co-brand partner card-portfolio is well-established in the public record (e.g. 2016 portfolio purchase from AmEx). The Visa-0 result is expected: Visa is the network rail and only names merchants when material to Visa's financials, not when material to issuer-side card portfolios. The 'Costco co-branded' phrase total of 10 is mostly Costco's own filings, which is the expected pattern for an issuer-side detail (Calibration 7: counterparty-disclosure threshold satisfied at the bank-counterparty level, not the network level). CONTROL-baseline PASS.

scores.claim_text: Lease portfolio: $4.21B lease assets / $4.15B liabilities; 20-yr operating / 25-yr finance lease tenor; total lease costs $618M FY25.
supports: edgar_fts.query_fulltext('Costco', cik=MAC) - 25 hits (from claim COST-2 query)
scores.M_check: Mall-REIT counterparty exposure + internal Note-5 lease disclosures

M_value.FY25_lease_cost_components: Operating $271M + Finance amortization $102M + Interest on finance lease liab $63M + Variable $182M = $618M total

scores.interpretation: Calibration 12 (lease-portfolio structural risk): Costco's lease portfolio is small RELATIVE to its $77B total assets and $5.8B long-term debt - operating lease ROU is just 3.5% of total assets. The 20-year operating-lease tenor is long-tail (consistent with retail-real-estate norms) but is well-disclosed in Note 5 with maturity ladder. The implied lease-payment stream is comfortably covered by $13.3B annual operating cash flow. SPG/MAC counterparty cross-references confirm Costco is a real tenant in the institutional CRE ecosystem. KPMG-audited disclosure. No M-side red flag - this is precisely the kind of HIGH-rubric, well-structured retail-lease disclosure that defines the CONTROL baseline. PASS.

scores.claim_text: $15.3B cash + ST investments; $13.3B FY25 operating cash flow; $5.8B fixed-rate LTD; $1.96B remaining buyback authorization; dividend raised from $1.16 to $1.30/share April 2025.
supports: filing self-disclosure (audited cash flow statement + Note 4 debt)
scores.M_check: No external M-source needed - audited financial statements with KPMG unqualified opinion; cross-internal consistency check vs prior-year filings

M_value.LTD_total: $5,805M all fixed-rate Senior Notes; no near-term refinancing risk (next maturity 2027)
M_value.dividend_action: Quarterly dividend $1.16->$1.30 April 2025 (+12.1%); 22 consecutive years of dividend increases per Costco's broader record
M_value.no_distress_markers: No going-concern qualifier; no covenant-waiver disclosure; no impairment of any material asset; no Form 15-12G/25-NSE; no ATM offering; KPMG opined ICFR effective

scores.interpretation: Calibration 10 (delisting/going-concern check for retail-distress cohort): all distress markers ABSENT. Cash position growing, operating cash flow accelerating, debt entirely fixed-rate and termed-out, ongoing buyback program funded out of cash flow, dividend being raised. This is the textbook CONTROL profile for the retail cohort - it is what 'healthy' looks like on every framework dimension. PASS.

scores.claim_text: Inventory DOWN $531M YoY ($18.65B->$18.12B) despite ~8% sales growth; $142M FY25 LIFO charge.
supports: filing self-disclosure (Note 1 inventory policy; segment-level inventory breakdown)
scores.M_check: No external M-source - audited segment-level inventory disclosure with cross-period consistency

M_value.implied_turn_improvement: Inventory turnover (COGS/avg inv) improving meaningfully - merchandise costs rose ~7.9% ($222.4B->$239.9B) on FLAT-to-DOWN inventory base
M_value.LIFO_charge_FY25: $142M (vs immaterial benefit FY24, immaterial charge FY23) - reflects modest inflation in merchandise cost basis

scores.interpretation: Calibration retail-9 / Calibration 12 (inventory turns vs benchmarks): Costco's inventory turn was already best-in-class (~14x at typical industry-vs-Costco comparisons); the FY25 figures show further improvement (sales up, inventory down). This is the OPPOSITE of the typical distress-retail pattern (excess inventory build, write-down risk). The LIFO charge is small ($142M / $239.9B COGS = ~6 bps) and reflects normal commodity inflation. CONTROL-baseline PASS. No M-side contradiction available or required.

summary.cohort_role: CONTROL - high-quality retail issuer with best-in-class disclosure; every claim corroborated either by external counterparty cross-disclosure (Citi/SPG/MAC) or by KPMG-attested internal financial statements. No distress markers triggered (Calibration 10): no going-concern, no covenant-waiver, no impairment, no ATM/dilution, no form-15/25-NSE. This is the calibration anchor against which the rest of the retail cohort should be measured.
